source_used: The Verge (Reuters original blocked); MassLive headline seen
key_facts: New York AG Letitia James is among 40 bipartisan attorneys general who filed a notice of interest in Character.AI's bankruptcy case
Character.AI announced Tuesday it was filing for Chapter 11 and selling some assets to Disney
The AGs warn of risk in transferring the technology because of the sensitive conversations, the many minors and features of the product
Several states had opened a probe in 2024 into consumer protection and privacy, after a lawsuit from the mother of a 14-year-old who died by suicide
They did not reach an agreement before the bankruptcy filing
They urge the judge to require any buyer to adopt age assurance, limits on minors, crisis safeguards and user data deletion
quote_evidence: James is among 40 bipartisan AGs who filed a notice of interest in Character.AI’s bankruptcy case “to put all parties on notice of the regulatory issues that will need to be addressed in any sale or transfer of the Debtor’s business or assets.”
“This company collected some of the most private thoughts children have ever shared, and now those conversations could be sold off to the highest bidder,” James said in a statement.
why_it_matters_hint: Chat logs of children could pass to a buyer unless the court sets conditions.
notes: Reuters original blocked (401); The Verge reported independently. Character.AI bankruptcy itself ran in our 14 Oct edition.
title: US states seek children's data protections in Character.AI bankruptcy
